slug: the_moon_comes_over_the_tower
title: The Moon Comes Over the Tower
blurb: Detective Daniel Whittaker arrives at the silent research station Skywatch-73 to find out why it stopped answering, and soon realizes he is not alone.
authors: Eve
season: T&L
format: prose
---

Daniel awoke, having finally arrived in the Ebrostim solar system. He dressed himself, making sure to grab his badge and his trusty sidearm. His trusty pistol had gotten him out of many different horrible situations; he never kept it far from his person. Grabbing a cup of coffee, Daniel checked in with the pilot of his small ship. “[Anything coming up on the scans?]{Daniel Whittaker}” grumbled Daniel. “[Nothing yet, the station’s silent]{Daniel's Pilot},” the pilot retorted. “[Any idea why?]{Daniel Whittaker}” “[You’re the detective here, Daniel.]{Daniel's Pilot}” The duo went silent as they pulled into the station. Daniel went back over his notes about this case. This was Skywatch-73, a station designed to scout out this solar system. There was some sort of anomalous activity with the star, too bright and too hot for a star of this size. Most of the planets in the system are charred, burnt rocks, with one having an unfinished report. Daniel was here to figure out why the station stopped responding to report requests.

The first thing he noticed stepping out of his ship was the main power was offline, leaving only the emergency backup generators. The landing bay was dim, illuminated by the emergency lights of the station. He produced his flashlight from a pocket and illuminated the docking area. There were no signs of any person, no escape attempts, no fights, just… nothing. Daniel pressed further into the building, while the pilot checked to see if there was anything they could find nearby. The echo of Daniel’s feet hitting the metallic floor was the only noise he heard, following the signs towards the generator room. He peeked into the room, certain that something was going to jump at him, but it never did. He entered and restarted the station’s primary generators. The station whirred to life, light flooding the station’s hallways and corridors. “[Did you find anything?]{Daniel Whittaker}” Daniel sent a message to his pilot. He waited, and received no response. “[Are you there?]{Daniel Whittaker}” He asked the receiver. “[Hey! Are you okay?]{Daniel Whittaker}” Daniel yelled into the microphone, growing worried. He ran back to the hangar, pistol at the ready. He only found a trail of viscera leading into a vent, a vent too small for him or the pilot to fit into.

Daniel knew there was something, or someone, on the hunt for him. He checked every vent, every corner, every possible angle of attack for whatever this killer was. His plan was to send out a distress call, warning the rest of the GU or whatever passing spacer was about this. He had the hope of someone, anyone giving him backup. He finally made it into the communications room; he set the broadcast strength to maximum, and grabbed the microphone. “[This is Daniel Whittaker, GU-appointed detective, badge number 152-161-1A5. I am broadcasting from Skywatch-73 in the Ebrostim system. All the staff are presumed dead; my pilot has been murdered by some unknown creature. If anyone can hear this please help!]{Daniel Whittaker}” Daniel backed away from the broadcasting equipment. His heart pounds as he hears uneven, dragging footsteps from outside the room. He turns around and finds the culprit for his pilot's murder.

The visage of this horrific creature struck pure terror into Daniel’s heart. The race of what it is could not be determined, looking almost like a melted humanoid. Sharp bloodstained claws jut out of its hands; the creature’s jaw was forcefully snapped into a harsh set of mandibles. Daniel didn’t waste a second; he aimed and fired at this creature, hitting it right between the eyes. It stopped, and then leapt at him. Daniel fired four more times as it flew at him. It crashed into the wall behind him; it dragged itself off the ground to continue its assault. Daniel emptied the rest of his magazine into the monster; the bullets barely even slowed it down. Daniel panicked and looked around, looking for anything that could potentially kill this creature. He spotted a flamethrower in the corner and dove for it, quickly grabbing it and immolating the beast. It let out an ear-piercing screech, and fell over, dead. Daniel picked himself off the ground, panting and shaking. As adrenaline slowly left his system, he found a recording from the station’s previous residents. He let it play, hoping it would give some answers.

“[This is Stephanie Burgess, lead researcher for Skywatch-73. We’ve made progress in our research into the Ebrostim anomaly. We can definitely conclude the star’s status is unnatural, as we found an ancient device that sent an unknown beam into it. We also found a swarm of solar panels surrounding the star, the energy being sent onto an asteroid that had an alien facility on it. No signs of who could’ve built it yet; the ground team we sent to Erebus has stopped responding. We brought some of the machines we found back onto the station for further testing. Stephanie Burgess signing off.]{Stephanie Burgess}” The recording faded out and then silence returned to the station. Daniel thought about what his next move would be; he didn’t want to stand around and wait to see if anything else would attack, so he headed for the security office. He gripped the flamethrower tight, still feeling the tension of the possibility of another attack.

The door to the security office was cut open, not by any monster, but by what looked like a plasma torch. Stepping inside, he found signs of a gunfight. Daniel found another recording, and desperate to find out what the hell was going on, he let it play. “[Okana Dømbne, security captain of the Skywatcher. Something’s got into the others. It started when they brought that damn artifact to the station.]{Okana Dømbne}” The sounds of firearms being loaded and a plasma torch beginning to cut through a door could be heard in the background. “[Stephanie used it to mutate some of the crew and brainwash the rest into believing that this was some sort of next step for evolution. I don’t know how that got in her head, but they’re outside the gate. I’m glad I’ve got most of the security team on my side, at least.]{Okana Dømbne}” A heavy door slamming onto the ground replays, and then a cacophony of gunshots rings. The recording abruptly cuts out, leaving Daniel alone.

Daniel needed to figure out what had happened to Stephanie, so he made his way to the lead researcher’s office. Entering the office, he finds ramblings drawn on a wall. Drawings of a planet, filled with screaming faces, underneath scrawled “IT’S ALIVE.” Snooping through Stephanie’s computer, he found some personal logs detailing the testing the researchers did on the artifact. The artifact caused biomass to merge together, becoming a single living entity. A sudden migraine halted Daniel’s research; he grasped his head, panting heavily. A deluge of bile shot out of his mouth, coating the floor in vomit. He heard a faint whisper. “[Join us.]{Erebus}” His eyes shot around, looking for whatever said it. He couldn’t find anything; all he found was an empty room.

Desperate for a way out, Daniel began to check for any form of escape shuttles. All but one of them had already been launched. Checking the flight plan, he saw they all went to one place: Erebus. Daniel looked out and saw the planet in all its glory. The pulsating mass was the culmination of this research, time, and energy. The solution to all life’s problems, perfect harmony. Daniel climbed inside the shuttle, set his location, and his voice joined the chorus of billions.
